newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP shares up on profit hopes, technicals.
newsitem.headline: BNP shares up on profit hopes, technicals.

text.p: Shares in French bank BNP were up three percent in late trade on Wednesday, buoyed by technical factors and hopes of strong full-year profits, dealers said.
By 1545 GMT, shares were up 3.01 percent at 236.40 francs in heavy volume of 1.7 million shares, outpacing the blue-chip CAC-40 index which was up 0.62 percent.

In early trade this morning, BNP broke through a key technical resistance level of 231 francs, triggering a buy signal that powered the share up five percent to hit 241 francs before it retraced some of its gains, dealers said.
"It's a good share, not too expensive, with strong medium-term growth potential," said Massonaud-Fontenay-Kevern analyst Jean-Marc Loiseau.
He had a six-month share price target of 280 francs and forecast profits of 3.4 billion francs in 1997, 4.1 billion in 1998 and 4.9 billion in 1999. In 1995, BNP had profits of 1.78 billion francs.
He said BNP's sale of 8.6 million of its own shares in the second half and in January 1997 had been weighing on the stock as had the sale by Axa-UAP of four million BNP shares.

"There's a general awakening in the market to the quality of BNP. It's one of the best shares in the sector, offering guarantees in terms of results, falling provisions and a strategy," said another analyst. He forecast profits of 3.35 billion francs in 1997, 3.78 billion in 1998 and 4.3 billion in 1999.
He added he believed talk about a possible reinforcement of links with Dresdner Bank or a tie-up with Paribas had some foundation even if he did not believe it would take place in the short term.
